This matters because these three states depend on Colorado River water for agriculture, municipal supplies, and hydroelectric power, and the cuts threaten economic stability, farm viability, and the region's ability to sustain its growing population amid climate change and prolonged aridification.

Residents in low-lying and previously damaged areas are the most exposed.
